key_insight: DLLM decoding wastes compute because only a small subset of tokens is decodable at each diffusion step; attention-derived token importance strongly predicts which tokens are decodable, enabling focused allocation of decoding compute.
problem_solved: Reduces wasted parallel compute in Diffusion Large Language Model (DLLM) decoding by identifying and prioritizing tokens that are actually decodable at each diffusion step.
method: Use attention-derived token importance to estimate per-token decodability during diffusion decoding.
Dynamically allocate decoding computation to high-importance (decodable) tokens and defer or skip non-decodable ones while retaining block-parallel processing.
Introduce a lightweight gating/scheduling mechanism (FOCUS) to route compute only where it yields progress, cutting redundant work across diffusion steps.
impact: Makes DLLM inference much more compute- and time-efficient, lowering inference cost and improving practicality of diffusion-based LLMs for deployment and research.

paper_title: FOCUS: DLLMs Know How to Tame Their Compute Bound
paper_authors: Kaihua Liang, Xin Tan, An Zhong, Hong Xu, Marco Canini
